takeaway: Splenectomy is done for unstable or high-grade splenic trauma, ITP, hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune haemolytic anaemia; in sickle cell sequestration crisis transfusion is preferred.

question.text: A splenectomy is indicated for all but which one of the following conditions?

lines.text: Which conditions need the spleen out, and which do not?
An injured spleen is managed conservatively for lower grades.
But if the patient is unstable, or the injury is above grade three, it comes out.
The green ticks are ITP, hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.
In all three, splenectomy is performed.
Sickle cell disease is the odd one out.
In an acute sequestration crisis there is little evidence for surgery over a blood transfusion.
